notes:
### Apportionment Formula
* **Fact:** Multistate business net income is apportioned using a **single sales factor** (gross sales / receipts), referred to as the Business Activity Ratio (BAR). For businesses selling tangible personal property, the apportionment ratio is the proportion of gross sales made within Iowa to total gross sales everywhere. 
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Code § 422.33(2)(b): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/ico/section/422.33.pdf
  * Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—503.5: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/rules?agency=701
  * Iowa Department of Revenue IA 1120 Instructions: https://revenue.iowa.gov/

---

### Sourcing of Services and Intangibles
* **Services:** 
  * **Fact:** Iowa applies **market-based / benefit-received sourcing**. Gross receipts from services are included in the numerator of the apportionment factor in the proportion to which the recipient of the service receives the benefit of the service in Iowa. If the recipient receives all the benefit in Iowa, 100% is sourced to Iowa; if only a portion is received in Iowa, receipts are sourced in proportion to the benefit received in Iowa.
  * **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
  * **Official Sources:** 
    * Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—503.6(1): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/rules?agency=701
    * Iowa Code § 422.33(2)(b): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/ico/section/422.33.pdf

* **Intangibles:**
  * **Fact:** 
    * *Business Investment Income / Royalties / Licensing Fees:* Sourced to the Iowa numerator to the extent the royalty or licensing asset is an integral part of regular business activity occurring in Iowa. If the intangible asset is not an integral part of regular business activity in or outside Iowa and an election to include it is made, the receipts are sourced to Iowa if the taxpayer’s commercial domicile is in Iowa.
    * *Capital Gains/Losses from Intangibles:* Operationally related business gains/losses are apportioned using the Business Activity Ratio; nonbusiness capital gains or losses from intangibles are allocated to Iowa if the taxpayer's commercial domicile is in Iowa.
  * **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
  * **Official Sources:** 
    * Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—503.2: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/rules?agency=701
    * Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—503.4: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/rules?agency=701

---

### Industries with Special Apportionment Formulas
* **Fact:** Specific industry apportionment rules are established under Iowa Administrative Code r. 701—503.6 and 701—503.7:
  * **Railroads:** Car and locomotive mileage ratio for freight and passenger revenue.
  * **Airlines, Truck and Bus Lines, Water Transportation, and Freight Car/Equipment Companies:** Proportion of mileage traveled in Iowa to total mileage traveled within and without the state.
  * **Pipeline Companies (Oil, Gasoline, Gas, etc.):** Proportion of Iowa traffic units to total traffic units.
  * **Telecommunications Companies:** Specific sourcing based on service transmission points (local service in state, intrastate toll in state, and interstate toll originating in state and billed to an Iowa service address).
  * **Radio and Television Broadcasters:** Proportion of Iowa population served by broadcasting to total population served (measured by recognized market survey).
  * **Publishers and Electronic Media/Broadcasting of Print Content:** Destination of subscriber/purchaser and circulation factor for advertising receipts.
  * **Electric & Gas Transmission Utilities:** Proportion of Iowa traffic units to total traffic units.
  * **Construction Contractors:** Proportion of gross receipts from contracts performed in Iowa to total gross receipts.
  * **Financial Organizations (Non-Exempt):** Special receipts numerator rules covering interest, fees, services, and operational gross income within Iowa.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:** 
  * Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—503.6: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/rules?agency=701
  * Iowa Admin. Code r. 701—503.7: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/rules?agency=701

---

### Form and Schedule Used to Compute Apportionment
* **Fact:** 
  * **Form IA 1120, Schedule E** (*Apportionment of Income*) is used to compute the Business Activity Ratio (BAR). The resulting apportionment percentage from Schedule E, line 13 is transferred to Form IA 1120, Step 5, line 8 ("Iowa percentage from Schedule E").
  * *(Pass-through entities use Form IA 1120S, Schedule E for S corporations and Form IA 1065, Schedule E for partnerships.)*
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:** 
  * Form IA 1120 (Form 42-001): https://revenue.iowa.gov/
  * IA 1120 Instructions (42-002): https://revenue.iowa.gov/

notes:
### 1. Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Nexus

* **What Creates Nexus:**
  * **Corporate Income Tax:** Imposed on every corporation "doing business in this state, or deriving income from sources within this state". "Doing business" is broadly defined to include all activities or transactions for financial or pecuniary gain or profit. Nexus is also established by owning or deriving income from real, tangible, or intangible property located or having a business or commercial situs in Iowa (e.g., trademarks, licensing, patents, loans, partnership interests).
  * **Franchise Tax:** Imposed on financial institutions "doing business within the state" and not exempt from federal income tax.
  * **Pass-Through Entity Ownership:** An out-of-state partner or S corporation shareholder establishes income or franchise tax nexus and an Iowa filing requirement by holding an ownership interest in a partnership or S corporation doing business in Iowa.
* **Economic Nexus / Bright-Line Thresholds:** 
  * **Not found.** Iowa has no factor-presence or bright-line economic nexus threshold (e.g., no specific dollar threshold of Iowa sales or property/payroll) for corporate income tax or franchise tax. The Iowa Department of Revenue explicitly notes that there is no filing threshold for business entities, meaning any entity doing business or deriving income from Iowa sources must file regardless of net income or revenue amount.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Department of Revenue – Out-of-State Businesses: https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-guidance/business-taxes/out-state-businesses
  * Iowa Code § 422.33 (Corporate Income Tax): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/ico/section/422.33.pdf
  * Iowa Code § 422.60 / § 422.61 (Franchise Tax): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/ico/section/422.60.pdf
  * Iowa Administrative Code 701—501.1 (Who Must File): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/agencies
  * Iowa Form IA 200 Instructions: https://revenue.iowa.gov/

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold & Measurement Period

* **Gross Revenue Threshold:** **$100,000** or more in gross revenue from Iowa sales.
* **Transaction Count Threshold:** **None** (Iowa's original 200-transaction threshold was repealed effective July 1, 2019 by 2019 Iowa Acts, HF 779).
* **Measurement Period:** The current calendar year or immediately preceding calendar year.
  * *Collection Timing:* A remote seller that did not exceed the threshold in the prior year but exceeds it during the current year must begin collecting sales tax on the first day of the next calendar month that begins at least 30 days after the date the threshold was met, continuing through the remainder of that calendar year and the entirety of the next calendar year.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Code § 423.14A(3): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/ico/section/423.14A.pdf
  * Iowa Administrative Code 701—207.1: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/agencies
  * Iowa Department of Revenue – Remote Sellers & Marketplace Facilitators: https://revenue.iowa.gov/remote-sellers-marketplace-facilitators

---

### 3. State's Stated Position on Public Law 86-272 Protection

* **Scope and Criteria:** 
  * Iowa acknowledges that under P.L. 86-272 (15 U.S.C. §§ 381–386), the state cannot impose a net corporate income tax if a foreign corporation's sole business activity in Iowa consists of the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property, provided orders are sent outside Iowa for approval or rejection and filled by shipment or delivery from a point outside Iowa.
  * Protection does **not** extend to domestic corporations, sales of services, leasing/licensing, or real and intangible property. It also does not protect independent brokers or manufacturers' representatives acting on behalf of others.
  * Iowa has not formally adopted the Multistate Tax Commission's (MTC) revised 2021 guidance regarding internet activities in its administrative rules.
* **Return Filing Requirement Despite Protection:** 
  * The Department maintains that P.L. 86-272 protection **does not relieve** an entity doing business in Iowa of its return filing obligations. 
  * An entity protected by P.L. 86-272 must still file an annual Iowa corporate return (Form IA 1120), check the P.L. 86-272 box, and report $0 tax due. Consolidated corporate groups must identify members asserting P.L. 86-272 protection on Schedule M.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Department of Revenue – Out-of-State Businesses: https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-guidance/business-taxes/out-state-businesses
  * Iowa Administrative Code 701—501.1(2) (Corporate activities not creating taxability): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/law/administrativeRules/agencies
  * Iowa Department of Revenue – IA 1120 Instructions (42-002): https://revenue.iowa.gov/

notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax Rate(s)
* **Tax Years 2025 & 2026:** Iowa imposes a single flat individual income tax rate of **3.8%** on all taxable income. (Under Iowa Senate File 2442, graduated brackets were eliminated and the flat rate took effect beginning January 1, 2025, remaining unchanged at 3.8% for 2026).
* **Official Sources:** 
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *IDR Announces 2025 Individual Income Tax Brackets and Interest Rates*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/press-release/2024-10-16/idr-announces-2025-individual-income-tax-brackets-and-interest-rates
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *IDR Announces 2026 Individual Income Tax and Interest Rates*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/press-release/2025-10-21/idr-announces-2026-individual-income-tax-and-interest-rates
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Iowa Tax Rate History*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/iowa-tax-rate-history

---

### 2. Corporate Income Tax Rate(s) & Minimum Tax
* **Tax Years 2025 & 2026 Rates:** The corporate income tax rates remain the same for both 2025 and 2026:
  * **$0 to $100,000:** 5.5%
  * **Over $100,000:** 7.1%  
  *(Note: Under Iowa Code § 422.33(1)(b), rate reductions trigger if net receipts exceed $700 million; the Department of Management determined the threshold was not met for either year, keeping rates unchanged)*.
* **Minimum Tax:** **None.** Iowa's corporate alternative minimum tax (AMT) was repealed for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2021.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Order 2025-02, Certifying Iowa Corporate Income Tax Rates for 2026*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/press-release/2025-10-21/idr-issues-order-related-tax-year-2026-corporate-income-tax-rates
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Iowa Corporate Income Tax Rates*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/business-income-tax/iowa-corporate-income-tax-rates
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *IA 1120 Instructions*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/forms/ia-1120-instructions-42-002

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax & Local Rates
* **State Sales Tax Rate:** **6%** (applies to both 2025 and 2026).
* **State Use Tax Rate:** **6%** (applies to both 2025 and 2026).
* **Local Option Sales Tax (LOST):** Local jurisdictions may impose an additional **1%** local option sales tax (raising the total combined rate up to 7% in participating jurisdictions). There is no local option use tax.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Sales & Use Tax Guide*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/sales-use-tax-guide
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Sales Tax*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/individual-taxes/sales-tax

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes
* **Franchise Tax on Financial Institutions:** Imposed on the net income of financial institutions (Iowa Code § 422.63):
  * **Tax Year 2025:** **4.1%**
  * **Tax Year 2026:** **3.8%** (decreased from 4.1% in 2025 pursuant to scheduled statutory phase-downs).
  * *Franchise Alternative Minimum Tax:* Repealed for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2021.
* **Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET):** Qualifying partnerships and S corporations may elect to pay tax at the entity level.
* **Gross Receipts / Margin Tax:** **Not found.** Iowa does not levy a general gross receipts or margin tax.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Iowa Tax/Fee Descriptions and Rates*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates
  * Iowa Department of Revenue - *Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)*: https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/business-income-tax/pass-through-entity-tax-ptet

notes:
### 1. Individual Returns: Due Dates and Extensions

* **Due Date:** Calendar-year individual returns are due on **April 30** following the close of the tax year (or the next regular business day if April 30 falls on a weekend or state holiday under Iowa Code § 421.9A).
* **Extension Rules:** 
  * Iowa does not have a separate extension application form; federal extensions do not automatically apply for Iowa filing purposes.
  * If a taxpayer pays at least **90%** of their total correct tax liability on or before **April 30**, an automatic 6-month extension to file is granted until **October 31** without incurring a late-filing penalty.
  * Any necessary extension payments must be submitted by April 30 electronically via GovConnectIowa or by mailing the Iowa Individual Income Tax Payment Voucher (**IA 1040V**). Interest continues to accrue on any tax paid after April 30.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax years 2025 and 2026**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [Iowa Department of Revenue - Individual Taxes](https://revenue.iowa.gov/individual-income)
  * [Iowa Department of Revenue - Note: Additional Information](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/1040-expanded-instructions/note-additional-information)

---

### 2. Corporate and Pass-Through Entity Returns: Due Dates and Extensions

* **C Corporation Return Due Date:** Calendar-year C corporation returns are due no later than **April 30** (the last day of the 4th month following the close of the tax year). Cooperative associations are due on or before the 15th day of the 9th month following year-end.
* **Pass-Through Entity Due Dates:**
  * **Partnership (IA 1065):** Calendar-year returns are due on or before **April 30**.
  * **S Corporation (IA 1120S):** Calendar-year returns are due on or before **April 30** (the last day of the 4th month following the close of the tax year).
* **Extension Rules:**
  * **C Corporations:** Taxpayers who pay at least **90%** of their correct tax liability on or before the original due date automatically receive a **6-month extension** to file (until October 31 for calendar-year filers) without late penalties. Payments are remitted via GovConnectIowa or Form **IA 1120V**.
  * **Partnerships:** If no Iowa tax is due, the entity automatically receives a **6-month extension** of time to file. If tax is owed (e.g., PTET), at least **90%** of the tax liability must be paid by the original due date to receive the 6-month extension without penalty.
  * **S Corporations:** A **6-month automatic extension** is available. If the S corporation owes built-in gains tax, passive investment income tax, or elective PTET, at least **90%** of the total tax liability must be paid by the original due date.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax years 2025 and 2026**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [IA 1120 Corporation Income Tax Instructions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-forms/ia-1120-instructions-42-002)
  * [IA 1065 Partnership Return Instructions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-forms/41-017-ia-1065-partnership-return-income-instructions)
  * [IA 1120S S Corporation Instructions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-forms/2025-ia-1120s-iowa-income-tax-return-s-corporation-instructions)

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)

* **Existence:** Yes. Enacted under Iowa Code § 422.16C, partnerships and S corporations may make an annual election to be taxed at the entity level.
* **Tax Rate:**
  * **Tax Year 2025:** **3.8%** (matches Iowa's flat individual income tax rate).
  * **Tax Year 2026:** **3.8%**.
* **How to Elect:** The PTET election is made directly on the entity's annual return (**IA 1065**, Part 5 / **IA 1120S**, Part 6) by checking the designated PTET election box. The election is irrevocable once made and applies only to that tax year.
* **When to Elect:** The election deadline is **six months after the original due date** of the IA 1065 or IA 1120S return (e.g., **October 31** for calendar-year filers). While the election may be made up to six months after the original due date, PTET liability must be paid by the original due date (April 30) to avoid penalties and interest.
* **Applicability:** Effective for tax years 2022 through years for which the federal deduction limitation under IRC § 164(b)(6) applies (includes 2025 and 2026).
* **Official Sources:**
  * [Iowa Department of Revenue - Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/business-income-tax/pass-through-entity-tax-ptet)
  * [IDR Modifies the Pass-Through Entity Tax Election Deadline](https://revenue.iowa.gov/newsroom/idr-modifies-pass-through-entity-tax-election-deadline)
  * [Iowa Tax/Fee Descriptions and Rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general-tax-guidance/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates)

---

### 4. Composite or Group Nonresident Returns for Pass-Through Entities

* **Mandatory Filing:** Under Iowa Code § 422.16B, pass-through entities (partnerships, S corporations, estates, trusts) with nonresident members are required to file **Form IA PTE-C** and remit composite tax on Iowa-source income on behalf of nonresident members.
* **Exemptions:** An entity is exempt from filing Form IA PTE-C if:
  * It makes a timely PTET election under Iowa Code § 422.16C for the tax year;
  * It is an eligible publicly traded partnership; or
  * It is prohibited under law from making distributions.
* **Electing Out (Nonresident Composite Agreement):** A nonresident member may be excluded from the composite return tax payment if the member and the pass-through entity sign the **IA Nonresident Member Composite Agreement (Form 41-175)** prior to the entity's return due date. The agreement is retained by the pass-through entity and presented only upon IDR request.
* **Composite Tax Rates:**
  * *Individuals, estates, trusts, partnerships, and S corporations:* **3.8%** for **2025 and 2026**.
  * *C corporations and UBIT-taxed entities:* **7.1%** for **2025 and 2026**.
  * *Financial institutions:* **4.1%** for **2025**; **3.8%** for **2026**.
* **Due Date:** Due on the same date as the entity's annual Iowa income tax return.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [Iowa Composite Returns for Tax Year 2022 and Later](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-guidance/iowa-composite-returns-tax-year-2022-and-later)
  * [Iowa Department of Revenue - Form 41-176 IA PTE-C Instructions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-forms/41-176-ia-pte-c-composite-return-instructions)
  * [Iowa Tax/Fee Descriptions and Rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general-tax-guidance/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates)

---

### 5. Estimated Tax Requirements and Nonresident Withholding

* **Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Throughs:** Under Iowa Code § 422.16B, standard pass-through entity nonresident withholding was replaced by the mandatory composite return (**IA PTE-C**) starting in 2022; pass-through entities do not withhold separate tax on a nonresident member's distributive share.
* **Individual Estimated Tax Requirements:**
  * **Tax Year 2025 Threshold:** Required if an individual expects to owe **$200** or more in Iowa income tax after credits and withholding.
  * **Tax Year 2026 Threshold:** Changed/raised to **$1,000** or more.
  * **Installments (Calendar Year):** Paid in four installments due on:
    * Installment 1: **April 30**
    * Installment 2: **June 30**
    * Installment 3: **September 30**
    * Installment 4: **January 31** of the following year
* **Business Entity & PTET Estimated Tax Requirements:**
  * **Threshold:** Business entities (C corporations) and pass-through entities electing PTET that expect to owe **$1,000** or more in Iowa tax must remit quarterly estimated payments.
  * **Installments (Calendar Year):** Due on the last day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the tax year: **April 30**, **June 30**, **September 30**, and **December 31**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [Iowa Department of Revenue - Estimated Income Tax Payments](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/estimated-income-tax-payments)
  * [Summary of Tax Year 2025 Form Changes](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/summary-tax-year-2025-form-changes)
  * [Estimated Income Tax Payments for Business Entities](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/business-income-tax/estimated-income-tax-payments-business-entities)

---

### 6. Main Return Forms

* **Individual:**
  * **IA 1040** (Iowa Individual Income Tax Return)
  * **IA 1040ES** (Individual Estimated Tax Payment Voucher)
* **Corporate:**
  * **IA 1120** (Iowa Corporation Income Tax Return)
  * **IA 1120ES** (Corporation Estimated Tax Payment Voucher)
* **Pass-Through Entities:**
  * **IA 1065** (Iowa Partnership Return of Income)
  * **IA 1120S** (Iowa Income Tax Return for S Corporation)
  * **IA 1041** (Iowa Fiduciary Return of Income)
  * **IA PTE-C** (Iowa Composite Return)
  * **Form 41-175** (Iowa Nonresident Member Composite Agreement)
  * **IA Schedule CC** (Composite and PTET Credit form for owners)
* **Applicability:** Applies to **tax years 2025 and 2026**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [Iowa Department of Revenue - Tax Forms](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-forms)
  * [IA PTE-C Composite Return Instructions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/tax-forms/41-176-ia-pte-c-composite-return-instructions)

proposals.snippet: A PTET election must be made by the date which is six months after the original due date for filing the IA 1065.

proposals.value: Pass-through entities with nonresident members must file Form IA PTE-C and remit composite tax unless electing PTET or obtaining signed Form 41-175 agreements. For 2025, the composite rate is 3.8% for individuals and pass-throughs, 7.1% for C corporations, and 4.1% for financial institutions.
proposals.snippet: ● Nonresident members who have completed the 2025 Nonresident Member Composite Agreement (41-175).

proposals.value: Pass-through entities with nonresident members must file Form IA PTE-C and remit composite tax unless electing PTET or obtaining signed Form 41-175 agreements. For 2026, the composite tax rate is 3.8% for individuals, pass-throughs, and financial institutions, and 7.1% for C corporations.
proposals.snippet: ● Nonresident members who have completed the 2025 Nonresident Member Composite Agreement (41-175).

proposals.value: For 2025, individuals must remit estimated payments if they expect to owe $200 or more in Iowa income tax after credits and withholding. Business entities and PTET filers expecting to owe $1,000 or more must pay quarterly estimates, while pass-through nonresident withholding is handled via Form IA PTE-C.
proposals.matched_title: Note: Additional Information | Department of Revenue
proposals.snippet: Estimated Payments Iowa Residents Iowa residents who expect to owe Iowa income tax of $200 ($1,000 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026) or more from income not subject to withholding tax must make estimated tax payments to avoid a penalty for underpayment of estimated tax.

proposals.value: For 2026, individuals, C corporations, and PTET-electing entities must remit estimated tax payments if they expect to owe $1,000 or more. Nonresident pass-through withholding is replaced by the composite return on Form IA PTE-C.
proposals.matched_title: Note: Additional Information | Department of Revenue
proposals.snippet: Estimated Payments Iowa Residents Iowa residents who expect to owe Iowa income tax of $200 ($1,000 for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026) or more from income not subject to withholding tax must make estimated tax payments to avoid a penalty for underpayment of estimated tax.

proposals.value: Individuals file Form IA 1040 and IA 1040ES, while corporations submit Form IA 1120 and IA 1120ES. Pass-through entities file Form IA 1065 or IA 1120S, along with composite Form IA PTE-C and Form 41-175.
proposals.matched_title: Iowa Composite Returns for Tax Year 2022 and Later | Department of Revenue
proposals.snippet: The composite return tax payment is due by the due date of the pass-through entity’s Iowa income tax return (IA 1065, IA 1120S, or IA 1041), not including extensions.
